# Live rich-text cutover + state echo suppression + concurrency conflict safety

## Context / Problem
This story **cuts the live Cloud and DC send paths over to the now-capable rich
codecs** (delivered by `e59d` and `271c`, on which this story depends) and makes
that cutover echo-safe. Because the DC codec is one-way and lossy, loop prevention
cannot rely on `decode(encode(x))==x`. Both clients must suppress echo by
**state**: compare the current Jira value against the last-synced baseline the
reconciler already keeps (ADR 0026, `binding_store.py:102`; `_BASELINE_FIELDS` at
`:108`; `set_baseline` at `:459`). We must also not silently destroy either side's
edits under concurrency — this story **reuses** the repo's settled concurrency
policy (story a713: local-wins + a deduped `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert
over the ADR-0026 baseline) rather than inventing a new arbitration — and any state
we add must respect epic `0303`'s churn discipline (a per-pass timestamp there
caused the tickets-store bloat this feature must not regress).

**Why the cutover lives HERE, not in the leaves.** `e59d`/`271c` deliver capable
codecs but deliberately leave the live send sites on the plain/identity path, so
that the observable format change and its echo-safety land **together** in one
story (this one), never a hazard-before-safety window.

## Prior art in this repo (build on the existing convergence + conflict machinery, do NOT re-invent it)
- **Three-way baseline arbitration already exists (ADR 0026, story d6bd).** The
  outbound diff compares the LOCAL ticket against a per-binding **baseline**
  (`binding_store.get_baseline`, mapped through the `InboundMapper` at
  `outbound_field_diff.py:193-197`) so a field is emitted only when local diverged
  from the last-synced Jira ancestor; `description` is one of the
  `_INBOUND_MIRRORED_FIELDS` (`outbound_field_diff.py:46`) and is already handled
  this way at `outbound_field_diff.py:273-293`. This story does NOT invent a new
  three-way merge — it makes that existing description compare rich-codec-aware.
- **Both-sides conflict detection + local-wins is ALREADY the settled policy
  (story a713).** When a mirrored field diverged on BOTH sides
  (`local != baseline` AND `remote != baseline`), `outbound_field_diff.py:354-362`
  appends `(jira_key, fname)` to the `conflict_sink`, which
  `run_differs.py:_emit_outbound_field_alerts` (`:97`) emits as a **deduped
  `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert** — resolution stays **local-wins** (rebar
  emits its value; the remote is never silently dropped, it is surfaced as the
  alert). This story REUSES that exact channel and policy for the body; it does not
  add a parallel LWW clock or a new conflict sink.
- **Once-only re-emit convergence already exists.** `outbound_field_diff.py:285-292`
  compares the fitted-local body to the RAW remote so a stale body re-emits exactly
  once, after which the landed body decodes to the normalized form and converges.
  For rich text this terminates iff the codec is idempotent under the compare —
  guaranteed by the codec law `normalize_outbound(t) == decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`
  (`test_rich_text_codec.py:163`, ticket a32a) plus the empirically-proven
  round-trip idempotence (marklas 99.65%). No observe-after-push GET is needed: a
  benign Jira re-canonicalization is absorbed by the decode-on-compare, then
  converges on the next pass.
- The rich-text COMPARE normalization is the codec's **`normalize_outbound`** op
  (`RichTextCodec`, `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py`), already routed through by
  `OutboundFieldMapper.map_fields_to_remote` (`outbound_mapper.py:77`),
  `outbound_fields.py:564`, and `inbound_differ.py:210`. This story makes those
  compares rich-aware; it does NOT add a second, parallel `norm()`.
- `binding_store.py` already persists the last-synced baseline via the always-on
  `_advance_baselines` (`reconcile.py:519`, run at persist `:600` from
  `ctx.curr_snapshot`); this story reuses that single writer unchanged.
- The codec law and the comment dedup that depends on it (`outbound_comments.py:48`)
  are preserved by routing every compare through the codec op.

## The live cutover (both clients — this story's new scope)
Reroute the direct plain-encode call sites through the capable codecs so the wire
actually carries rich text, and prove convergence:
- **Cloud:** repoint the four `AdfCodec` ops to the Markdown-aware `adf.py`
  functions (`to_wire→markdown_to_adf`, `decode_inbound→adf_to_markdown`,
  `normalize_outbound→adf_to_markdown∘markdown_to_adf`,
  `fit_outbound→fit_markdown_to_adf_limit`) and install the whole-codec plain-text
  fallback, updating the pin test at `test_rich_text_codec.py:198/205/207/208`.
  Then reroute the live consumers to the Markdown-aware path: the encode at
  `adapters/jira/acli.py:205` and `acli_cli_ops.py:369`, the fit at
  `jira_fields.py:53`, and the direct `adf.normalize_description` /
  `adf.fit_text_to_adf_limit` compare sites at `outbound_fields.py:564` and
  `inbound_differ.py:210` — **paired so the send-fit and the compare-fit are the
  identical transform** (the once-only re-emit convergence invariant). Each
  already-synced description re-emits **exactly once** (the `outbound_fields.py:564`
  once-only re-emit mechanism) to upgrade to rich ADF, then converges.
- **DC:** wire the pure `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki` (from `271c`) into
  `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`, and **redefine `WikiTextCodec.normalize_outbound` to the
  compare form `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))`** so the codec law
  (`test_rich_text_codec.py:163`) is re-established for the rendering codec. Because
  DC's live send composes `normalize_outbound(fit_outbound(value))` at
  `outbound_mapper.py:77`, this redefinition is exactly what makes
  `issue.update(fields=…)` begin shipping rendered wiki — the cutover — so it
  **must** land here with echo-safety, not in the leaf. **The DC CREATE path is a
  SEPARATE, explicitly-enumerated codec consumer:** `_map_local_to_dc_fields`
  (`backend.py:70`) constructs its OWN `WikiTextCodec()` and builds
  `"description": codec.fit_outbound(...)`, applying **only `fit_outbound`, never
  `to_wire`** — so redefining `to_wire`/`normalize_outbound` alone does NOT render
  on create. This story changes `_map_local_to_dc_fields` to render before the fit
  (compose the renderer/`to_wire` with `fit_outbound`) so a newly-created DC issue
  ships rendered wiki too. Update the DC identity pin tests
  (`test_wiki_normalize_is_identity`,
  `test_wiki_codec_wire_shape_and_decode_are_the_plain_string`,
  `test_non_string_values_pass_through_untouched`) to the rendering behavior.
- **Rollback:** the cutover is gated behind a single switch (config/flag) that
  restores the plain/identity path for that client without reverting the codec
  capability, so a bad rollout is one revert, not a code rewrite.

## Approach (echo-safety + concurrency — REUSE the existing baseline + conflict machinery)
Echo-safety and concurrency for the body are **already implemented** by the
ADR 0026 three-way baseline diff and the story-a713 both-sides conflict channel
(see Prior art). This story's job is to make that existing description path
**rich-codec-aware and provably convergent**, not to build a new merge:

1. **Rich-aware compare.** The description compare at
   `outbound_field_diff.py:273-293` already fits the local body and compares it to
   the remote; after the cutover the fit/compare run through the Markdown-aware
   codec (`normalize_outbound` = `adf_to_markdown∘markdown_to_adf` for Cloud,
   `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` for DC). Because the send-fit and the compare-fit
   are the **identical transform**, an already-synced body re-emits **exactly
   once** to upgrade to rich, then converges (the existing once-only re-emit
   mechanism, now codec-idempotent by the codec law).
2. **Baseline stays the single existing writer.** No observe-after-push GET and no
   second baseline writer are added: `_advance_baselines` continues to advance the
   per-binding baseline from `ctx.curr_snapshot` at persist. A benign Jira
   re-canonicalization of the rich body is absorbed by the decode-on-compare (step
   1) rather than by re-reading the pushed value, so the per-key
   succeeded-mutation plumbing the earlier draft required is unnecessary.
3. **Baseline/compare normalizers must compose.** The stored baseline is
   canonicalized on READ through the same `InboundMapper.map_remote_to_local` the
   compare uses (`outbound_field_diff.py:197`), and the rich codec's decode is that
   mapper's body path — so `decode(baseline_wire)` and the compare's
   `decode(remote_wire)` are the identical normalizer; an AC asserts a re-emitted
   body equals its own stored-then-decoded baseline (no normalizer mismatch).
4. **Concurrent both-sides edit → the EXISTING local-wins emit + conflict alert +
   additive inbound merge (all unchanged).** When `local != baseline` AND
   `remote != baseline` on the body, the outbound emit stays the settled
   **local-wins** (rebar's body is emitted) and the divergence is surfaced on the
   **existing `conflict_sink` → `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert**
   (`outbound_field_diff.py:354-362` → `run_differs.py:97`). The INBOUND apply
   keeps description in its existing **"additive"** conflict class
   (`conflict_resolver.FIELD_CLASSES` / `_field_contract.FIELD_CONTRACT`,
   `resolve_additive` — "conflicts merge additively, never overwrite"), so neither
   side's content is destroyed and no registry reclassification (and no
   `_field_contract` parity break) is introduced. This story adds nothing to the
   conflict registries; it relies on description already being a mirrored field in
   that conflict scan and already being additive on inbound.

**Origin-gating so Jira-native constructs survive (AC5).** Outbound is gated on
rebar-origin: a description update fires only when `local` differs from `baseline`
(a rebar-side edit). When a Jira author adds a native construct with no Markdown
source (a panel/mention/date — constructs `adf.py` already decodes at `:164/219`)
between passes and rebar made no edit, that pass sees `remote != baseline` but
`local == baseline`, so origin-gating emits **no** outbound and the construct
survives untouched. Only a genuine rebar-originated body change re-encodes (and a
concurrent both-sides edit is surfaced as the local-wins conflict alert above,
never a silent clobber). For the rich layer, store a
change-gated `rich_sha = sha256(rendered_wire)[:16]` (8 bytes) **inline** in the
binding (proven 0.07 KB/version stable, identical to the baseline profile; a
per-pass timestamp was proven to reproduce 0303's 12.62 KB anti-pattern) so a
re-render is only pushed when the wire actually changed. The compare stays
comparison-only and never writes back.

## Scope
- `adapters/jira/rich_text_codec.py` — Cloud cutover: repoint the four `AdfCodec`
  ops to the Markdown-aware `adf.py` functions + install the whole-codec fallback.
- `adapters/jira/acli.py` (`:205`), `adapters/jira/acli_cli_ops.py` (`:369`),
  `adapters/jira/jira_fields.py` (`:53`), `adapters/jira/outbound_fields.py`
  (`:564`), `inbound_differ.py` (`:210`) — Cloud live cutover through the
  Markdown-aware path (gated).
- `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_rich_text_codec.py` (`:198/205/207/208`) —
  update the Cloud pin test to the Markdown-aware delegation; update the DC identity
  pin tests + codec-law test for the now-rendering `WikiTextCodec`.
- `adapters/jira_family/rich_text.py` — DC cutover: `WikiTextCodec.to_wire`
  delegates to `wiki_render.render_markdown_to_wiki`; `normalize_outbound` set to
  `decode_inbound(to_wire(t))` (re-establishes the codec law for the rendering
  codec) — this is what makes `outbound_mapper.py:77` ship rendered wiki.
- `adapters/jira_datacenter/backend.py` (`:70`) — DC CREATE-path: change
  `_map_local_to_dc_fields` (today `codec.fit_outbound(...)` only) to render via the
  renderer/`to_wire` before the fit, so create ships rendered wiki (gated).
- `binding_store.py` — inline change-gated `rich_sha` beside the existing baseline
  (`_BASELINE_FIELDS`).
- `outbound_field_diff.py` (`:273-293`, `:354-362`) — make the EXISTING description
  compare rich-codec-aware and confirm `description` is covered by the existing
  both-sides `conflict_sink` scan; reuse `_advance_baselines` unchanged (no
  observe-after-push GET, no `_apply_mutations` change).
- the existing description differ / compare path — reuse the ADR-0026 three-way
  baseline diff + the story-a713 local-wins + `conflict_sink` conflict channel + the
  existing additive inbound merge (no `FIELD_CLASSES`/`_field_contract` change), plus
  **origin-gating** (outbound only when `local != baseline`, so a Jira-native
  construct authored with no rebar edit survives); reuse the codec
  `normalize_outbound` (NOT a new `norm()`, NOT changing the shared plain-text
  `inbound_fields.normalize_rich_text`).
- `tests/` — cutover, convergence, echo, conflict, and no-churn tests.

## Testing
- **Cloud convergence:** after the cutover, a converted ADF description posts once,
  and a second reconcile pass emits **zero** description updates (`test_cloud_cutover_converges`).
- **DC convergence:** a rendered-wiki description posts once and a second pass
  emits zero description updates (`test_dc_cutover_converges`).
- Self-echo: a rebar-originated body change propagates exactly once and a second
  pass pushes nothing (0 echo-back).
- Concurrent: both sides edit the same body; the pass keeps rebar's body
  (local-wins) and appends the divergence to the existing `conflict_sink` so an
  `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert fires — the remote value is recorded, not
  silently discarded (`test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`).
- Normalizer composition: a body re-emitted through the codec equals its own
  stored-then-decoded baseline (`decode(baseline_wire) == compare-normalized
  local`), so no normalizer mismatch re-emits forever (`test_baseline_decode_composes`).
- Origin-gating: a Jira author adds a native panel/mention to a synced description
  and rebar makes no edit; the next pass emits zero outbound and the construct
  survives verbatim (`test_jira_native_construct_survives`).
- No-churn: a pass with no body change updates 0 `rich_sha` entries and writes no
  timestamp; asserted by the git-delta cost harness (≤0.07 KB/version stable).
- Rollback: with the cutover flag off, the wire reverts to the plain/identity
  encode for that client (`test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain`).

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] After the Cloud cutover, a converted ADF description posts once and a second
  reconcile pass emits zero description updates; verified by
  `test_cloud_cutover_converges`.
- [ ] After the DC cutover, `issue.update(fields=…)` receives rendered wiki (not
  raw Markdown) and a second pass emits zero description updates; verified by
  `test_dc_cutover_converges`.
- [ ] The description compare reuses the codec `normalize_outbound` and the ADR-0026
  baseline diff, adding no parallel normalizer, and a re-emitted body equals its
  stored-then-decoded baseline; verified by `test_echo_uses_codec_normalize` and
  `test_baseline_decode_composes`.
- [ ] Outbound fires only on a rebar-originated change (`local != baseline`); the
  baseline is advanced by the single existing `_advance_baselines` and a benign Jira
  re-canonicalization converges within one re-emit without a re-GET; verified by
  `test_echo_rebar_origin_only` and `test_recanonicalization_converges`.
- [ ] A Jira-authored native construct (panel/mention/date) survives a subsequent
  rebar-originated reconcile pass under origin-gating; verified by
  `test_jira_native_construct_survives`.
- [ ] A concurrent both-sides body edit keeps rebar's body (settled local-wins) AND
  raises the existing `outbound-field-conflict` bridge alert so the remote value is
  recorded, never silently destroyed; verified by `test_concurrent_conflict_alerts`.
- [ ] The rich layer stores a change-gated inline 8-byte `rich_sha` and no
  per-pass timestamp, changing 0 entries on a no-op pass; verified by the
  git-delta cost harness reproducing the ≤0.07 KB/version stable profile.
- [ ] The cutover is flag-gated and reverts to the plain/identity wire when off;
  verified by `test_cutover_rollback_restores_plain`.
